method: Authorized low-resolution local videos were sampled at ASR-selected times. Every listed frame was inspected at original resolution and hashed after copying into the skill.
global_limit: A sampled still can verify visible subjects, depth, focus state, lighting appearance and UI overlays at that instant. It cannot prove camera movement, edit causality, focus transition, sound, lens/exposure values, creator intent or model-independent audience response.

items.title: How Kubrick, Spielberg, and Inarritu Stage their Scenes

frames.observation: Four people form a horizontal group; the central person gestures while the far-right person looks down. The colored diagram is an overlay.
frames.limit: Does not prove who moves or the gesture's target.

frames.observation: Three people form a triangle; the center back-facing figure partially occludes the space between two side-facing people.
frames.limit: Does not prove dialogue power or the preceding transition.

frames.observation: At least five people are distributed across a corridor in foreground, middle and background; newspapers and furniture create visible directional shapes. Pink dotted lines are overlays.
frames.limit: Overlay lines and still positions do not prove eye movement.

frames.observation: One standing figure with a long cane contrasts with several seated figures, producing visible height and directional differences. Colored lines are overlays.
frames.limit: Does not prove intimidation or movement.

frames.observation: At least three physical people occupy a narrow dressing room across depth; a mirror adds reflected figures and a back-facing foreground body creates occlusion.
frames.limit: Reflections may duplicate apparent people and do not establish physical locations alone.

frames.observation: Three physical people remain distributed in front/middle layers in the dressing room; the right foreground back blocks part of the center figure.
frames.limit: Does not prove an entrance or the removal of an occluder.

frames.observation: A blonde woman occupies foreground left while two people are layered behind among racks and mirrors.
frames.limit: Does not prove reveal order, reaction timing or who entered.

items.title: How Back to the Future Uses Perfect Blocking to Tell the Story

frames.observation: Two foreground people stand shoulder-to-shoulder while a clock-tower building remains clearly visible behind them.
frames.limit: Does not prove prior entry or later movement.

frames.observation: A damaged silver car dominates foreground/middle while one small standing figure appears at the left rear; an animation panel occupies the right side.
frames.limit: Only the person-car state is visible; animation dots do not prove motion.

frames.observation: One woman faces away in a bedroom, with bed and furniture defining foreground and background layers.
frames.limit: Does not prove a transition between planes.

frames.observation: A central couple has close hand-to-face contact while at least one additional person passes in the right background; a white target graphic is an overlay.
frames.limit: Does not establish the attention sequence or movement path.

frames.observation: A crouching woman and standing man occupy separated middle positions with street activity behind them.
frames.limit: Does not prove who redirected attention or changed position.

frames.observation: Two men face each other across a yard; the left man gestures and the eyeline axis is readable.
frames.limit: Does not prove a long-take transition.

frames.observation: Two men align front-to-back along a corridor depth axis; one is foreground left and the other centered behind.
frames.limit: Does not prove walking speed or the number of blocking positions.

frames.observation: One man occupies the center foreground while the corridor depth remains visible and another person is absent from frame.
frames.limit: Does not prove when or where the other person exited.

items.title: Depth of Field Explained: Ultimate Guide to Camera Focus [Shot List Ep. 4]

frames.observation: An astronaut and the distant Earth edge are both visibly detailed in a cold, high-contrast composition.
frames.limit: Does not prove lens or aperture values.

frames.observation: Two astronauts and spacecraft detail remain readable across depth, showing a deep-focus appearance.
frames.limit: Does not prove physical focus technique.

frames.observation: A flower is sharp while city lights behind become large warm circles, showing shallow focus and bokeh appearance.
frames.limit: Does not prove focal length or aperture.

frames.observation: A woman's face is sharp in close-up while the interior background is distinctly soft.
frames.limit: Emotional effect remains interpretation.

frames.observation: A boy and surrounding lights have low sharpness and visible glow, supporting a soft-focus appearance.
frames.limit: Does not identify a filter or prove intentionality.

frames.observation: A central masked person is sharp while side/foreground people are heavily soft in a hospital corridor.
frames.limit: A still proves only one focus state, not rack direction or speed.

frames.observation: A black-background diagram shows a camera and several subject planes with colored lines.
frames.limit: Diagram presence does not prove real optical rendering.

frames.observation: A warm interior image contains severe motion blur and no stable focus plane.
frames.limit: Does not prove tilt-shift; retained as a counterexample to inferring focus type from blur.

items.title: Roger Deakins on "Learning to Light" — Cinematography Techniques Ep. 1

frames.observation: Upward tree branches against overcast sky show cool-gray diffuse light and broad detail across depth.
frames.limit: Does not prove weather causality or settings.

frames.observation: A restaurant booth uses warm red-purple environmental color with a readable figure and interior layers.
frames.limit: Does not prove the intended emotion.

frames.observation: A low-angle tricycle image under overcast light has low contrast and clear environment depth.
frames.limit: Does not prove exact camera height or lens.

frames.observation: A black-and-white close-up retains face and meter detail while the background is softer; highlights and shadows remain separated.
frames.limit: Does not reveal the actual exposure reading.

frames.observation: A dark interior figure is backlit from a bright left window, with deep shadows and retained corridor depth.
frames.limit: Does not prove exposure values.

frames.observation: A behind-the-scenes group surrounds a camera in neutral warehouse light.
frames.limit: Does not prove the lighting result in a finished shot.

frames.observation: A tabletop still life retains product color and window highlight detail under directional daylight.
frames.limit: Does not prove meter strategy.

frames.observation: A warm practical light dominates a deep corridor with a back-facing figure and dark preserved spatial layers.
frames.limit: Does not prove the number or type of sources.

items.title: Editors on Editing: Downsizing - Kevin Tent, ACE

frames.observation: A finished-film medium shot shows a woman in a bright room holding a dark rectangular object.
frames.limit: One frame cannot prove performance continuity, VFX repair or cut logic.

frames.observation: Kevin Tent speaks in interview framing with raised explanatory hands.
frames.limit: Supports speaker context only, not the claimed edit effect.

frames.observation: The same interview subject shows a concentrated or puzzled expression.
frames.limit: Does not show the letter-reading scene or its duration.

frames.observation: A second interview participant listens with a slight smile.
frames.limit: A listener pose does not prove the film's reaction cut.

frames.observation: The second participant gestures while speaking.
frames.limit: No NLE timeline or scene transition is visible.

frames.observation: Kevin Tent laughs with a strong visible reaction.
frames.limit: Does not prove the trigger, reaction length or edit point.

frames.observation: The second participant touches his chin in a thoughtful listening pose.
frames.limit: Does not prove audience testing or pause duration.

frames.observation: Kevin Tent speaks with both hands framing an explanation.
frames.limit: No timeline, tracks or timing comparison is visible.
